title: Attention pathway hasher for heterogeneous kernel allocation
creator: Ava Martinez
summary: Introduce a compact per-request fingerprint (hash) of attention characteristics to map requests to pre-bundled kernel implementations across heterogeneous GPUs, improving p95 latency and reducing kernel-switch overhead without increasing tail variance.
description:
Problem statement:
The runtime currently picks kernels primarily based on architecture + sequence length buckets. We observe cases where requests with similar sequence lengths but different attention patterns (sparsity, head variance, key/query norms) have markedly different optimal kernels. This leads to suboptimal p95 latency and unnecessary kernel context switches during mixed workloads.

Proposal in one sentence:
Compute a compact attention-pathway fingerprint per request at prefill time and use a lightweight hasher to select a kernel bundle (kernels + launch params) optimized for that fingerprint and the target hardware. Maintain an online cache and a grace fallback for unseen fingerprints.

Why this is novel/valuable:
- Captures request-level attention geometry not represented by seqlen alone.
- Enables stable kernel choices for heterogeneous mixes (chat + long-context summarization) with lower tail latency.
- Supports gradual online learning: bundle scores updated by observed latency/regret metrics.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full neural predictors or an expensive ML model in the hot path. We aim for a deterministic lightweight hash + small lookup table and an asynchronous tuner that updates the table.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can compute attention-pathway fingerprint at prefill in < 0.25ms median on x86-based CPU sidecar for 2k token context
Fingerprint->bundle lookup and kernel switch decision adds <1ms median overhead and <3ms p95 for typical requests
End-to-end p95 improves by >=6% compared to baseline for mixed workloads in simulated production traffic (see metrics_benchmarks)
Fallback path exists: unseen fingerprints are mapped to architecture+seqlen default and logged for online tuning
Can run shadow experiments updating bundle scores without affecting production routing (shadow flag & metrics only)
design_notes: Fingerprint composition: small fixed-size vector combining: head-wise energy ratio histogram (4 buckets), query/key L2-normalized variance (1 scalar bucketized), token-level sparsity proxy (top-k attention mass fraction), and position-embedding drift estimate. Total bits target: 64 bits after quantization/hash.
Hasher: XXHash64 with custom salt per GPU-family to avoid cross-arch collisions; hashed value maps to 256-entry bundle table (configurable).
Bundle contents: preferred kernel implementation id, launch params (smem, threadblock), prefetch stride, KV-cache placement hint (local/shared), and performance prior (latency mean/variance).
Table lifecycle: LRU with TTL; asynchronous tuner observes execution outcomes and updates priors via exponential moving average. Updates are batched and pushed to the control plane every minute.
Safety: if bundle selection causes >2x expected latency on first 5 samples, automatically disable bundle for that fingerprint for 10 minutes and mark for manual review.

Compatibility: quantized kernels might be unsuitable for certain attention patterns; bundle metadata includes 'quantization_safe' boolean and runtime will fallback if model is served in a non-quantized mode.
Telemetry: emit fingerprint id, bundle id, chosen kernel id, observed latency, GPU occupancy, and decode step when enabled by customer (opt-in).
experiment_plan: Baseline collection: sample 24 hours of production traffic and record attention-derived stats per request (no routing changes). Produce offline clusters to validate fingerprint discriminativity (2 days).
Prototype: implement hasher + in-memory bundle table in staging runtime; one Canary region routes 1% traffic via fingerprint lookup with conservative TTL and shadow updates (2 weeks).
Metrics: compare p50/p95 latency, 99th latency, throughput, GPU SM utilization, and kernel-switch rate. Additionally track bundle cold-start count and disable events.
A/B: 2-week A/B comparing standard seqlen-based policy (control) vs fingerprint routing (variant); measure customer-impacted latency and error rates.
Rollback criteria: any customer-visible error spike >0.2% absolute or p95 regression >5% triggers immediate rollback to control for Canary region.
tasks: T1: Instrument attention statistics extraction at prefill (Rohan) - implement lightweight collectors and unit tests
T2: Implement attention-pathway hasher + bundle table (Ava) - in-memory, thread-safe, with TTL and LRU
T3: Add bundle metadata schema to runtime config and console (Design: Lina) - display bundle hit rates and priors
T4: Async tuner service to aggregate execution outcomes and update priors (Enginfra: Mateo) - batching + safety limits
T5: Shadow/Canary wiring and flags (SRE: Priya) - 1% rollout automation
T6: E2E benchmarks and synthetic mixes (Bench: Jae) - create chat/long/qa mixtures and run regression harness
T7: Docs PR and runbook for bundle disable/triage (PM: Sophie)
metrics_benchmarks: Baseline (control): p95=134ms, p50=18ms, kernel-switch-rate=0.9/s on mixed workload
Target (after feature): p95<=126ms (>=6% improvement), p50 within +/-5% baseline, kernel-switch-rate reduced by >=30%
Operational: bundle hit rate >=60% on steady-state traffic after 24h tuning
risks: Fingerprint collision causing incorrect kernel choice for diverse requests; mitigation: conservative TTL + disable on high regret
Telemetry volume increase if enabled broadly; mitigation: sampling + per-customer opt-in
Edge cases where attention proxies misrepresent compute characteristics (e.g., models with custom attention variants); mitigation: model whitelist and per-model overrides
Increased codepath complexity in hot path could affect median latency; mitigation: microbenchmarks and CPU budget target (0.25ms overhead)
rollout_plan: Week 0: Baseline telemetry collection and offline analysis
Week 1: Staging prototype + internal perf tests
Week 2: Canary 1% in us-west with monitoring + shadow updates
Week 3: Expand to 10% if metrics meet targets, continue tuning
Week 4: Full production rollout gated by SRE sign-off and no unresolved disables
